body:
Every `safe-tier-1` docs PR this cycle has needed a manual `gh pr merge --admin`
despite green CI and a `success` run of `auto-merge.yml`. Observed twice on
2026-08-07: #1450 (opened by the 20:00Z tick, still open and green at 22:22Z)
and #1452 (opened and stalled in the same tick that filed this).

## Mechanism — all four links OBSERVED

1. `auto-merge.yml` evaluates the tier and calls `gh pr merge --auto --squash`,
   which enables GitHub's *native* auto-merge. The run reports `success` — it
   enabled the setting, which is all it claims to do.
2. The `main protection` ruleset (id `15871246`) sets
   `strict_required_status_checks_policy = true`, i.e. a branch must be
   up to date with `main` to merge.
3. `main` receives commits on its own — the `Update Translations` bot is the
   routine one — so an open PR goes `BEHIND` shortly after it is opened.
4. Native auto-merge does **not** update the head branch. Nothing else does
   either. So the PR sits green + `BEHIND` indefinitely.

`gh pr view` reports `mergeable=MERGEABLE` throughout, which is what makes this
easy to miss: the blocking condition shows up only in `mergeStateStatus=BEHIND`.

## Why it matters

The CHANGES-SHA backfill is the last step of every release cycle, and it is
always tier-1, so it always lands in this hole. Each one then needs a human or
a tick to notice and admin-merge it. A tick that does not look will leave the
ledger un-backfilled, which is the record the *next* release reads.

## Options

- Have `auto-merge.yml` call `gh pr update-branch` before enabling auto-merge,
  and re-run on `push` to `main` so it re-updates. Closest to the intent.
- Enable the repo's "Automatically update branch" / auto-update setting so
  GitHub keeps auto-merge candidates current.
- Drop `strict_required_status_checks_policy` for docs-only paths — narrowest
  in effect but weakens the gate for everything sharing the ruleset.

Noticed while shipping #1451 and #1452.
title: tier-1 auto-merge stalls forever once a PR goes BEHIND
